sources.citation: Robert B. Cialdini, Joyce E. Vincent, Stephen K. Lewis, Jose Catalan et al. (1975). Reciprocal concessions procedure for inducing compliance: The door-in-the-face technique. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1975) in Journal of Personality and Social Psychology establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Robert B. Cialdini, Karen Ascani (1976). Test of a concession procedure for inducing verbal, behavioral, and further compliance with a request to give blood. Journal of Applied Psychology.
sources.notes: Demonstrates that reciprocal concessions boost actual blood-donation attendance and future volunteering.

sources.citation: Thomas Hugh Feeley (2025). 50-Year review of the Door-in-the-Face message strategy. Communication Monographs.
sources.notes: Thomas Hugh Feeley (2025) peer-reviewed review in Communication Monographs examining 50-Year review of the Door-in-the-Face message strategy.

sources.citation: Thomas Feeley, Ashley E. Fico, Allison Zorzie Shaw, Seyoung Lee et al. (2017). Is the Door-in-the-Face a Concession? Communication Quarterly.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2017) in Is the Door-in-the-Face a Concession? Communication Quarterly extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: John C. Mowen, Robert B. Cialdini (1980). On Implementing the Door-in-the-Face Compliance Technique in a Business Context. Journal of Marketing Research.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1980) in Journal of Marketing Research extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Daniel J. O'Keefe, Scott L. Hale (2001). An odds-ratio-based meta-analysis of research on the door-in-the-face influence strategy. Communication Reports.
sources.notes: Meta-analytic test establishing boundary conditions (same requester, prosocial request, short delay) for Door-in-the-Face compliance.
